full_judgment: 40. In Hadkinson vs Hadkinson, (1952) 2 All ER 567, a decree Nisi was granted to the mother by which she was given the custody of the child with direction that the child should not be removed out of the jurisdiction of the Court without its sanction. By arrangement between the parties it was agreed that the father should have reasonable access to the child. The decree was made absolute. The mother remarried and without the sanction of the Court, she removed the child to Australia where she was living with her present husband. The father of the child applied to the Court for an order that the mother should bring the child back within the jurisdiction. The application was allowed. The mother made an appeal before the Court of Appeal. The Counsel for the father took the preliminary objection that the mother was not entitled to be heard because she was in contempt. For the mother it was contended that she was entitled to appear and resist the application notwithstanding her contempt, and, the order having been made, she was equally entitled to be heard on an appeal against the order.
